title: Heart Rate Response to Physical Activity Using a Wearable ECG and 3-Axis Accelerometer Under Free-Living Conditions
content: Recent advances in wearable sensing technology have enabled simultaneous measurement of heart activity and body movement using devices equipped with both ECG recording and 3-axis accelerometers. This study examined whether transient heart rate (HR) responses to physical activity can be accurately characterized under free-living conditions. Continuous RR interval data and activity levels derived from accelerometer signals were analyzed using a multivariate autoregressive (MVAR) model. Results from 12 participants showed a strong correlation between predicted and observed HR responses (r² = 0.93, r = 0.96, p &lt; 0.001). These findings indicate that up to 93% of transient HR dynamics associated with daily physical activity can be explained by the model. The approach provides a promising framework for noninvasive, continuous monitoring of cardiovascular responses in everyday health and wellness applications.
